title: Scheduling, quality gates and the money plan

say: Scheduling, quality gates and the money plan.
This is the video for module 2 of Bulk Production Planning.
Most late deliveries are decided on the first day, when the producer starts too late.

say: So you will build three plans: a backward schedule, quality gates, and a cash plan.

panel.heading: Late, faulty or unaffordable: plan it out
items: Most late deliveries start on day one

say: Backward scheduling starts from the delivery date and subtracts every stage. For example, Kemi must deliver 5,000 packs of plantain chips on Thursday 10 December.

panel.heading: Count back from the delivery date

say: The day before, she counts cartons, does the final quality check and prepares documents.

panel.heading: Count back from the delivery date

say: Before that, 2 buffer days, kept empty for power cuts, sickness or a bad batch.

panel.heading: Count back from the delivery date

say: Production is 11 working days at her proven rate, so it starts on Tuesday 24 November.

panel.heading: Count back from the delivery date

say: The day before, a short first-article run checks that the line matches the golden sample.

panel.heading: Count back from the delivery date

say: Printed pouches take 10 working days, so they must be ordered by Tuesday 10 November, a full month before delivery.
Count working days only. A plan that quietly counts Sundays is late before it starts.

panel.heading: Count back from the delivery date
panel.rule: Count working days, not calendar days.

say: Put 25, 50, 75 and 100% milestones on a wall sheet, and fill in actual good packs each evening. The gap column is the most important number.

panel.heading: Watch the gap every evening
items: Gap under 5%: recover in normal hours
Gap 5 to 10%: extra time at the bottleneck
Over 10% or buffer half used: call buyer

say: After three days Kemi is 70 packs behind, about 5% of plan. That is easy to recover now.

panel.heading: Watch the gap every evening
items: Gap under 5%: recover in normal hours
Gap 5 to 10%: extra time at the bottleneck
Over 10% or buffer half used: call buyer

say: A bigger gap needs planned extra time at the bottleneck only, within safe working hours.

panel.heading: Watch the gap every evening
items: Gap under 5%: recover in normal hours
Gap 5 to 10%: extra time at the bottleneck
Over 10% or buffer half used: call buyer

say: If the gap passes 10%, or half the buffer is used, call the buyer the same day with the facts and a revised plan.
Buffer days are the buyer's protection. Do not plan to use them.

panel.heading: Watch the gap every evening
items: Gap under 5%: recover in normal hours
Gap 5 to 10%: extra time at the bottleneck
Over 10% or buffer half used: call buyer

say: Quality gates are planned checkpoints, each with a clear measure and a rule for a fail. Gate 1 checks each delivery against specification.

panel.heading: Five gates through the run

say: Gate 2 compares the first units of each day with the golden sample, before full speed.

panel.heading: Five gates through the run

say: Gate 3 checks a small sample at a fixed interval, for example 5 packs every 100 packs, for weight, seal, colour and taste.

panel.heading: Five gates through the run

say: Gate 4 counts good units and rejects at the end of the day.

panel.heading: Five gates through the run

say: Gate 5 draws a sample from different cartons before loading.
And hygiene never slows down for deadlines. Handwashing, hair covers and clean surfaces are never skipped, and anyone with diarrhoea or vomiting stays away from food handling.

panel.heading: Five gates through the run

say: Kemi fills to 103 g so normal variation stays above the 100 g on the label. On day 4, check 4 finds 2 of 5 packs underweight.

panel.heading: Day 4: a scoop that held less
items: Cause: new scoop, fills about 99 g
Refill the 11 under 100 g and log it

say: Her stop rule says: if 2 or more of the 5 sampled packs fail, stop that station.

panel.heading: Day 4: a scoop that held less
items: Cause: new scoop, fills about 99 g
Refill the 11 under 100 g and log it
panel.rule: 2 or more fails in 5 packs: stop, find the cause, then restart.

say: The cause: the weigher changed scoops after lunch, and the new scoop holds less.

panel.heading: Day 4: a scoop that held less
items: Cause: new scoop, fills about 99 g
Refill the 11 under 100 g and log it
panel.rule: 2 or more fails in 5 packs: stop, find the cause, then restart.

say: She returns to the marked scoop, re-weighs the last 100 packs, and refills the 11 under 100 g. The problem stayed inside 100 packs, not thousands.

say: Now the money. Cost the run from the quantities you will actually buy, after rounding up.
Kemi's materials come to about 2,561,300 naira. Labour, including 2 training days for temporary workers, is 328,000. Gas is 275,000.
Delivery is 60,000 and the trial run 20,000.
Direct cost is 3,244,300 naira. She adds a 5% contingency, so the full cost is about 681 naira per pack.
At a bulk price of 950 naira, profit is about 28% of revenue. A price of 700 would have left almost nothing.
Kemi pays for pouches, plantain and wages for weeks before the balance comes in. List every payment by date. The lowest running balance is your cash gap.

panel.heading: Profit is not cash

cards.d: List every payment in and out by date. With a 40% deposit, Kemi's lowest balance is about minus 1,344,300 naira.
A 50% deposit cuts the gap by 475,000 naira. Staged payment is another option.
A deposit counts only when it shows in your account. Not a screenshot or SMS alert.

say: Ask for a bigger deposit, or staged payment, for example 40% on order, 30% when the buyer approves the first-article packs, and 30% on delivery.

say: And never order printed pouches on a promise. Fake transfer screenshots are common.

say: Accept only if the schedule fits with buffer, the price leaves your margin, and you can cover the cash gap. If one fails, negotiate before you say yes.

panel.heading: Say yes only when all three work
items: The price leaves your margin after contingency
You can cover the cash gap
Keep a quality log as evidence
